newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Franklin Resources plays down Scitex speculation.
newsitem.headline: Franklin Resources plays down Scitex speculation.

text.p: Mutual funds manager Franklin Resources Inc indicated on Thursday that the six percent stake in Scitex Corporation it acquired recently is not intended to be used in a takeover bid for the Israeli company.
"There is no intention beyond what is in the filing," a Franklin spokeswoman said by telephone from California.
She was referring to its February 13 filing to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission stating that its holding in Scitex had reached 2.55 million shares, or six percent of equity.
The shareholding is held through Templeton Investment Council Inc which acts as an adviser to Franklin's Templeton funds, the filing said.
News of the acquisition spurred speculation in the Israeli media that it was part of an impending takeover bid for Scitex, a maker of digital printing equipment.
Asked if Franklin was acquiring the shares for a third party, the spokesman said: "I can't confirm or deny it." She said there was no precedent for such an action by Franklin.

Speculation about a possible takeover of Scitex rose after the company last week reported continued losses in the fourth quarter of 1996. Scitex said its net loss was $24.6 million for the quarter or $0.57 a share, bringing the full-year loss to $178.3 million, or $4.16 a share.
Scitex said it was continuing its restructuring plan. Some analysts have expressed scepticism.
"I am not convinced it's turning yet," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.

Last April, Scitex was subject to a hostile takeover bid from an American-Israeli entrepreneur, Davidi Gilo, who made offers of between $20 and $25 a share. Scitex's principle shareholders rejected the offer at the time.
Gilo was unavailable for comment on Thursday. Officials from Israel's Discount Investment Corporation, one of the main shareholders, were also unavailable.

James Melican, an International Paper executive who represents IP on the Scitex board, could not be reached for comment. International Paper IP.N holds 13 percent of Scitex. (( -- Jerusalem newsroom 972-2-5370502))
